components.nav-bar.height.supportingText: SAP's web surface is built like an application frame rather than a marketing site. A 60px bar in `{colors.chrome}` sits across the top, and on any product or services page a second rail drops beneath it carrying a breadcrumb and a row of tabs. That two-storey chrome is the first thing the design commits to: before a visitor reads a headline they have been told where they are in a very large catalogue, and the page below behaves like the content pane of that catalogue.
components.nav-bar.height.reason: The same pinned prose explicitly supplies px units for this component height.

components.hero-band.height.supportingText: Hero treatment is the clearest per-template difference. The home page runs a full-bleed navy gradient, the services page a flat `{colors.primary-deep}` band at 450px, and the product page no band at all — just centred type on `{colors.canvas}` above an illustration. Three templates, three hero strategies, one chrome.
components.hero-band.height.reason: The same pinned prose explicitly supplies px units for this component height.

On touch widths the inactive tabs are the first thing that should grow.
